title: Storage classes: standard, nearline, coldline and archive

videos.script: Lesson 1 put Quitanda's files in a bucket and never asked what kind of shelf they sat on. {{shelf}} Every object in Cloud Storage has a storage class. Standard is the default, and three others cost less to keep: Nearline, Coldline and Archive. {{classes}} The catch is the door. The cheaper the shelf, the more it costs to take something back off it, and the longer you are billed for, even if you leave early. {{door}} What the door never costs is time. Every class answers in milliseconds, and you will read an archived file back at once. {{read}} You will also write one file into four classes, and watch the emulator ignore half of what you ask. {{ignore}} Then a short program prices a tebibyte for a year in São Paulo, in each class, and counts the reads it takes to lose the saving. {{year}} By the end you can look at a set of files, ask how often they are read and how long they stay, and name their class. {{end}}
